summary: Carlo Giussani was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Turin, Pisa, and the Scuola Normale Superiore under Bardelli, Weber, Roth, Ascoli, and Spiegel, he taught at Liceo Manin (1866–1874) and the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1874–1900).

Carlo Jamelle Harris specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Chengchi University, completing a Master of Arts in Philosophy under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carlo Puini was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Pisa from circa 1858 to 1862 and was appointed extraordinary professor of East Asian history and geography at the University of Florence in 1877.

Linguist Carlo Salvioni studied at Basel and Leipzig (PhD under Karl Brugmann). He held posts at the University of Turin (1885–1889), University of Pavia (1890–1902), and Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1902), succeeding Graziadio Isaia Ascoli.

Carlos Garcia-Jane works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Barcelona, Aberystwyth, South Wales, and Edinburgh (PhD 2022). His posts include bibliographer at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (2018) and book reviews editor for Buddhist Studies Review (2023).

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai. She lectured at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and served as Folklore Society president (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos (~1958–1964). She served as professor at the University of Buenos Aires and vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2018).

Carmen Meinert works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001, worked as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008), and joined Ruhr University Bochum (CERES) in 2013.

Carol A. Breckenridge was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1970 to 1976 and later held a post at the University of Chicago from circa 1982 to 2001.

Carol S. Anderson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson, later serving as guest professor at Hamburg (2018–2026) and Oslo (2026).

Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and completed her doctorate in philosophy at the University of Hamburg in 2006.
Carole M. Cusack is a scholar in religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Sydney (1988–1995) and became Professor of Religious Studies there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. After studies at Colgate and Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, she joined the University of Colorado Boulder in 2001, serving as Assistant Professor of Anthropology (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of Central Asian studies and religion. She studied at Cambridge and Leeds under Edmund Leach, held fellowships at Girton and King's College, and served as a university teacher at Cambridge from 1978 to 2010.

Caroline Rhys Davids was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UCL under George Croom Robertson, T. W. Rhys Davids, and Reinhold Rost. She lectured at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933), and edited the Pali Text Society (1907–1942).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned doctorates at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and at Wichita State University (2002–2004), later serving as Director at the University of Kansas in 2017.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.

Carsten Colpe was a scholar of religious and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Hans Heinrich Schaeder (~1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1962–1969) and the Free University of Berlin (~1969–1997).

Caterina Conio was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at Florence, Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, and Banaras Hindu University under Paul Hacker and T. R. V. Murti, teaching Indian religion and philosophy at the University of Pisa in 1974.
